events.credibility_reason: Attribution conflict: the 2026 survey describes Sokolin's 1940 contribution as a conjecture, not a proof; primary papers not read. The equal-square result itself is not disputed.

why: The statement asks for the value of F(Q²) for mixed-size squares, so every pre-snapshot result on it (Radó's 1/9, Ajtai's <1/4, BDJ's 0.1179 and 1/4−1/384) moves a bound rather than settling the value. Ajtai's family refutes Radó's 1/4 conjecture, but the statement asks for the value and does not assert 1/4, so I scored it as a bound with null object role. Equal squares is a restriction of the statement, so it is a case. Of the in-window items: Dall'Ara 2025 is an all-dimension asymptotic that by its own account gives nothing at d=2, so it is none for this problem. The survey only restates results (none). Xie–Ge restricts to translates (equal sizes), which changes the question, so it is a variant; the 2/13 is the researcher's arithmetic and in any case applies only to equal squares. No AI system did any of the mathematics. Wolfram Alpha in the survey is computer algebra.
doubts: The survey's footnote 7 (1/8 for two sizes, Mirsky's 8/63) remains unresolved; read as upper bounds, those figures would contradict the stated record. I take them to be guarantees, as the researcher does. Ajtai's 1/4−1/1728 figure rests only on Wikipedia.
